UnrealIRCd distribution tarball backdoored for RCE

Target: unrealircd · website
Date: 2009-11-10 to 2010-06-12 (214 days)
Actor: Individual Hacker (person)
Target Kind: daemon
Language: C
Cause: compromised_infrastructure
Motive: unauthorized_access_control
Transitive: false
Impact: backdoor, remote_code_execution
User Impact: 0
Phase: distribution

Synopsis

The official UnrealIRCd 3.2.8.1 source distribution was replaced on project mirrors around November 10, 2009 and remained exposed until June 12, 2010. The injected code disguised itself behind DEBUGMODE3 logic and executed arbitrary commands with the daemon user's privileges when a client sent input beginning with AB.

Story

Around November 10, 2009, UnrealIRCd 3.2.8.1 source mirrors were replaced with a tarball containing a backdoor. The substitution was not discovered until June 12, 2010, leaving a seven-month window in which users who built the IRC server from project mirrors could deploy attacker-modified source. LWN noted that official Windows binaries were not affected, but the project had not yet provided signatures that would have made the swap easier to detect.

The source change was disguised as `DEBUGMODE3` logic. When input began with `AB`, `DEBUGMODE3_INFO` matched and `DEBUG3_LOG` ultimately called `system()`, executing the rest of the client-supplied command as the user running the daemon. The DailyDave thread preserved the attacker-facing lore around the trigger, while LWN captured the larger lesson: unsigned source distribution left a project mirror network able to turn ordinary build practice into remote command execution.
